Lessons.Title: The $n^{\text{th}}$ Term
ExplanationParagraphs: Interpret equivalent explicit n-th-term formulas, including exponential factors and indexing offsets.

The recursive form f(n)=2f(n-1) with f(1)=3 has explicit form f(n)=3*2^(n-1) for integers n>=1. The same function can be written as (3/2)*2^n on the same domain. In repeated paper slicing, 80 square inches reduced to one fourth of the previous piece per stage yields A(1)=80 and A(n)=80*(1/4)^(n-1). Using exponents avoids iterating through every earlier value, but the stated domain is constrained by the physical model.

KeyConcepts.Title: Explicit term rule
KeyConcepts.Definition: A formula for term n uses n without earlier terms.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent expressions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Algebraically different formulas can define equal values.

KeyConcepts.Title: Domain matters
KeyConcepts.Definition: Sequence indices are positive or nonnegative integers according to the model.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not interpolate a fractional number of cuts.

WorkedExamples.Title: Paper slicing
WorkedExamples.Question: A(1)=80 and each new piece has one-quarter the area. Find A(4).
WorkedExamples.Check: Physical model requires a feasible step count.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating a sequence rule as context-free.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It can alter the index, initial term, units or learning target.
CommonMistakes.Correction: State the beginning term, domain and original lesson model.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using a fixed common difference when the sequence is not arithmetic.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Differing consecutive differences invalidate the arithmetic formula.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Calculate two or more differences or ratios before selecting a rule.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Auto-grading graphs, card exchanges or manipulative proof from a number alone.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Numeric equality does not establish a correct diagram or explanation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a teacher rubric for visual and reasoning evidence.
